name: Tin glazing
summary: A pot is dipped in a glaze with tin oxide in it. The glaze dries to a white, opaque coat on which a potter paints with oxides before the glaze firing.
how: Fire the pot once to a biscuit at about 950 °C.
Dip the biscuit in a bath of glaze with 5 to 10 % tin oxide, so that the coat is about 0.5 mm thick.
Paint on the dry raw glaze with cobalt, copper, manganese or antimony.
Fire the glaze at about 1000 °C, so that the colours sink into the glaze.

origin.note: Abbasid potters add tin oxide to lead glaze to copy white Chinese porcelain.

adoptions.via: Luca della Robbia covers terracotta sculpture with white tin glaze, so that church reliefs stand in the weather.
Italian potters paint cobalt labels on the white tin glaze of drug jars made for the shelves of pharmacies.
Urbino painters brush whole scenes on the raw tin glaze before the firing, so that the colours sink into the glaze.
